peer_results.rationale: AVGO candidates discuss government sales funding, export controls, and compliance costs, but do not address risks related to M&A regulatory approval delays or termination fees for specific acquisitions comparable to AMD's ZT Systems disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Acquisitions and divestitures carry risks such as failure to advance strategy, operational disruption, inability to obtain approvals, and failure to realize returns, evidenced by a $2.9 billion goodwill charge related to Mobileye in Q3 2024. Additional risks include integration difficulties, compliance issues, and equity dilution or debt issuance.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel disclose risks that their respective strategic transactions or acquisitions are subject to obtaining government or regulatory approvals, and failure to do so can prevent completion or delay the transaction. AMD specifically cites the ZT Systems acquisition and a $300 million termination fee if approvals are not obtained, while Intel broadly states that failure to obtain required government approvals is a risk associated with its strategic transactions.

sentences.text: Our ability to complete the acquisition of ZT Systems is subject to closing conditions, including the receipt of consents and approvals from government authorities, which may impose conditions that could adversely affect us or cause the acquisition to not be completed.
We would be required to pay ZT Systems a termination fee of $300 million if the Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances related to the failure to obtain required regulatory approvals.

▪failure to complete a transaction in a timely manner, or at all, due to our inability to obtain required government or other approvals on a timely basis or without materially burdensome conditions or mandated acquisitions, divestitures, or disposals, IP disputes or other litigation, difficulty in obtaining financing on terms acceptable to us, or other unforeseen factors;

peer_results.rationale: MU candidates discuss government incentives (grants/subsidies) and IP licensing risks, which are distinct from M&A regulatory approval risks and transaction termination fees found in AMD's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA may not realize the potential benefits of business investments or acquisitions, may fail to successfully integrate acquired companies, and faces risks related to regulatory approvals, integration challenges, and investment volatility. Specific risks include difficulty in integrating technology and employees, assumption of liabilities, amortization expenses, debt issuance, equity dilution, and exposure to cybersecurity risks or loss of relationships. Past integration experiences have involved lengthy and costly systems integration and operational delays, which have impacted and may continue to impact results of operations. Additionally, investments in private and public companies carry risks of illiquidity, impairment losses, sector concentration, and failure to achieve returns.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA identify the difficulty or inability to obtain regulatory approvals as a key risk in completing acquisitions, which could reduce anticipated benefits or prevent closing. AMD focuses on the specific ZT Systems deal and potential termination fees, whereas NVIDIA notes that delays in obtaining regulatory approvals can prevent timely completion and that regulators may impose conditions that reduce the value of acquisitions.

sentences.text: We cannot assure you that we will receive the necessary regulatory approvals at all or in a timely manner or that closing conditions will be satisfied.

Our ability to complete the acquisition of ZT Systems is subject to closing conditions, including the receipt of consents and approvals from government authorities, which may impose conditions that could adversely affect us or cause the acquisition to not be completed.

If we are unable to timely complete acquisitions, including due to delays and challenges in obtaining regulatory approvals, we may be unable to pursue other transactions, we may not be able to retain critical talent from the target company, technology may evolve and make the acquisition less attractive, and other changes can take place, which could reduce the anticipated benefits of the transaction and negatively impact our business.
Regulators could also impose conditions that reduce the ultimate value of our acquisitions.
